newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANI says Ellicott report due end of April.
newsitem.headline: ANI says Ellicott report due end of April.

text.p: Engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said on Tuesday it is expected to receive a report into its controversial acquisition of German environmental business ABT from media baron Kerry Packer.
"We have been by advised by Ellicott that it will be the end of April," ANI group manager of corporate affairs Frank Sufferini told Reuters.

ANI bought the ABT business through its German based environmental group Holter from Packer, who at the time was ANI largest shareholder after launching a A$1.40 per share takeover offer in April 1989.
Ellicott was commissioned by the ANI board following pressure last year by former shareholder Ross Palmer, who called for an investigation into the ABT acquisition.
ABT was mainly responsible for the A$233.6 million writedown in the Holter unit in the 1995/96 year due to cost overuns and delays associated with ABT's waster to energy projects.
Packer's family company Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd sold its controlling stake in ANI two weeks after it sold ABT to ANI.
Ellicott, a former Australian attorney-general and federal judge, has travelled to Germany to talk to Holter executives and to Consolidated Press.
The report was orginally due late last year, but was delayed due to Ellicott's ill health.
